name: Oil Slick
pitch: A thin-film rainbow over dark anodised metal; every panel shows a different colour.
reference: Thin-film interference: soap bubbles, oil on wet tarmac.
verdict: realistic as a custom flip wrap
fit: fixed: bands halved and driven by the geometric normal (orange peel had made them jagged), withheld on panel creases
r4_note: Reads instantly as thin-film rainbow over dark metal on every colour and angle; no seams or broken logos visible, convincing oil-film look.

name: Frozen
pitch: Matte metallic: a dusty, desaturated face with a fine grain, a soft silver rim and a broad satin sun sheen.
reference: BMW Individual Frozen paints; Bugatti satin finishes for the sheen.
fit: rebased gloss-metal 29 -> matte 28 so it finally loses the clearcoat mirror; broad metallic sheen; grain fades by pixel footprint
r4_note: Only slightly duller than gloss; white unchanged, no visible grain or satin sheen. Fix: stronger desaturation and lift, kill sharp reflections, visible grain, broader silver rim.

name: Fluoro
pitch: Day-glo paint that looks brighter than the light hitting it, now keeping more of its shading.
reference: F1 flo-vis aero paint and fluoro liveries.
r4_note: High pixel diff but only a slight saturation lift; white is unchanged and red barely glows. Fix: raise the emissive floor so shadowed faces stay bright, boost saturation further.

name: Burnt Titanium
pitch: Heat-tinted titanium: blue nose, purple middle, straw-gold tail.
reference: Titanium oxide colours: gold, purple, blue with thickness.
fit: rebased chrome 27 -> satin metal 29: the mirror no longer magnifies jagged panel joins; livery divided out
r4_note: This is the most distinct finish. The blue-to-purple-to-gold gradient reads at every angle, with no seams. The gold tail is slightly pastel, so a touch more metallic straw would help.

name: Holo Flake
pitch: Prismatic flake: sparse coloured sparks over dark metal, rainbow streaks on lit panels.
reference: Rolls-Royce Spectre Lunaflair.
verdict: drop: duplicates holographic 41 / flake 34; sparse prism sparks shimmer

name: Bare Aluminium
pitch: Polished bare aluminium: warm grey metal, livery colour ignored.
reference: Mercedes-Benz W196 silver arrow.
r4_note: Clear silver on blue/red, but on Haas white it is near-identical to gloss. Fix: darker, warmer grey base, stronger env reflection contrast, faint brushed anisotropic streaks.

name: Raw Carbon
pitch: Unlacquered carbon weave: cool graphite satin over the livery.
reference: Koenigsegg Regera Naked Carbon (KNC).
fit: weave is the shipped carbon weave
r4_note: At 1:1 the weave and satin sheen are there and it separates from ultra black; at a glance it reads as a black car. Fix: lift the base toward graphite grey and widen the satin sheen so the weave reads at distance.

name: Flo-Vis
pitch: Glowing yellow-green aero-paint streaks running back along the body, gone at the nose.
reference: F1 flow-vis paint in testing.
fit: thin streak lines that fade to their mean coverage under ~3 px per period, so no crawl in motion
r4_note: The streaks read as contour loops, not flow lines running back along the body, and they nearly vanish on the white Haas. Fix: make the streaks run nose to tail and darken them on light bases.

name: Carbon Fade
pitch: Livery above the sidepod line, bare weave below, with a ragged edge between.
reference: Williams FW47; also RB22 and AMR25.
fit: neutral weave (was livery-tinted), torn edge from smooth noise not hash blocks, raised to the sidepod line; weave fades by footprint
r4_note: The split between livery and dark lower body reads, but the lower half is flat black with no visible weave or ragged edge, so it looks like rawcarbon or ultrablack. Fix: add weave contrast and a sheen, and roughen the edge.

name: Silver Fade
pitch: Silver nose dissolving through a halftone of dots into a black tail.
reference: Mercedes W17.
fit: dot screen printed per panel plane (top panels had stripes), anti-aliased dot edges, neutral black tail (was dark red)
r4_note: Silver-to-black fade reads clearly on all three liveries and angles, but the halftone dot band is invisible at race distance. Fix: enlarge the dots and widen the transition band.

name: Metal Flop
pitch: Metallic paint with a bright face and dark flop at the edges.
reference: Aston Martin AMR25 green; Williams FW48 blue.
fit: flop from the geometric normal, withheld on creases: no outline round every panel
r4_note: Indistinguishable from gloss at a glance on all three colours. Fix: much darker flop toward silhouettes, brighter face, add fine metallic sparkle; white base needs a grey flop.

name: True Matte
pitch: Chalky matte that goes lighter and greyer toward the edges, like a rough surface.
reference: Red Bull matte navy, 2016 onward.
fit: fixes shipped matte ~ gloss: capped below any highlight, greyed, shadows lifted
r4_note: It is barely distinguishable from gloss at any angle, so the owner would say they look the same. Fix: remove the specular highlight fully and strengthen the chalky grey lift toward the edges.

name: Pearl White
pitch: Tri-coat white: warm on the face, cool at the edge; livery colour ignored.
reference: Rolls-Royce Phantom Syntopia pearlescent.
r4_note: It turns the blue and red cars white, but on the white Haas it is nearly identical to gloss, and the warm-face/cool-edge flop is not visible. Fix: raise the warm/cool flop contrast.

name: Race Worn
pitch: Brake dust and rubber streaked back along the low bodywork.
reference: End-of-race dirt on the lower body. No photo in the library.
verdict: drop: dirt is a wear layer, not a paint finish

name: JPS Gold
pitch: Gloss black with sparse gold flake.
reference: John Player Special black and gold (Radford Type 62-2 JPS).
fit: base is now true gloss black set before lighting (was the livery dimmed: dark red); flake fades by footprint
r4_note: Clearly different, but reads as an all-over bronze-brown wash, not gloss black with sparse flake. Fix: deep black base, far sparser, smaller, brighter gold flakes.

name: Test Camo
pitch: Black and white dazzle camouflage; livery colour ignored.
reference: Dazzle wraps on pre-launch test cars. No photo in the library.
verdict: drop: sine blobs do not read as a real camo wrap and break at panel joins

name: Gold Foil
pitch: Crinkled gold heat-shield foil; the glints move as the view moves.
reference: McLaren F1 engine bay; F1 exhaust and floor heat shielding. No photo in the library.
verdict: drop: a whole body in heat-shield foil is not a real finish; mirror base magnifies joins

name: Anodised Blue
pitch: Dyed electric-blue anodised aluminium; highlights stay blue, with a pale grazing sheen.
reference: Dyed anodised aluminium parts. No photo in the library.
verdict: drop: composite panels are not anodised; reads as candy 35

name: Ceramic Bronze
pitch: Warm satin brown with a fine ceramic speckle and a broad soft sheen.
reference: Cerakote H-148 Burnt Bronze coating. No photo in the library.
verdict: drop: Cerakote is not body paint; duplicates satin 26 with a tint

name: Engine-Turned
pitch: Jewelled aluminium: offset rows of polished discs, each with a bright bow-tie.
reference: Pre-war GP dash panels; the Spirit of St. Louis cowl. No photo in the library.
verdict: drop: a jewelled whole body is not real; planar projection breaks at joins

name: Chromated Magnesium
pitch: Blotchy brown, olive-gold and green-grey cast metal with grain.
reference: Dow 7 chromated magnesium castings. No photo in the library.
verdict: drop: cast-magnesium blotches on body panels are not real

name: Ghost Pearl
pitch: Livery colour on the face; a complementary pearl tint shows only at sunlit edges.
reference: House of Kolor ice / ghost pearls. No photo in the library.
fit: pearl moved off the silhouette onto the sheen skirt and mid flop, withheld on creases
r4_note: Only a faint purple tint on wing edges; face and side-on look identical to gloss. Fix: stronger complementary pearl tint over a wider sunlit-edge band, visible on white too.

name: Xirallic
pitch: Dense, sharp white crystal glints that twinkle as the view moves.
reference: Merck Xirallic aluminium-oxide platelets. No photo in the library.
fit: glints fade by footprint (no shimmer at 10-26 m); a crisp white lustre carries it at hero distance
r4_note: A few glints on the blue graze cell only; red and white look like gloss. Fix: denser, larger, brighter white crystal glints, visible on light bases too.

name: Mystichrome
pitch: Green to cobalt to purple to black across viewing angles; livery colour ignored.
reference: 2004 Ford SVT Cobra Mystichrome; ChromaFlair pigment. No photo in the library.
r4_note: Unmistakable on all colours, but hues sit as flat per-panel pastel blocks with no black flop. Fix: smooth per-pixel angle ramp, deepen saturation, add black at grazing.

name: Midnight Purple
pitch: Near-black purple with a violet sun bloom that turns bronze at the edges.
reference: Nissan R34 GT-R Midnight Purple III. No photo in the library.
r4_note: In sun it reads as bright magenta or pink, not near-black purple, and the bronze edge flip is not visible. Fix: darken the base, shift the bloom to violet, and add a bronze tint at the edges.

name: Ultra Black
pitch: About 1% reflectance: the car reads as a silhouette; livery colour ignored.
reference: BMW VBX6 in Vantablack VBx2 (Surrey NanoSystems). No photo in the library.
r4_note: It reads as a near-black silhouette on all three liveries, with logos intact. The top-panel highlights could be flattened further so it separates more from rawcarbon.

name: Rain Soaked
pitch: Wet paint goes deep and dark, a water sheet mirrors the sky on top, beads glint.
reference: Wet-race paint. No photo in the library.
verdict: drop: a weather state, not a finish (belongs to the wet-race look)

name: Stealth Stripes
pitch: Matte body with gloss twin stripes and a gloss flank band.
reference: Red Bull matte years against its gloss RB22.
verdict: iterate later: coordinate-box stripes do not follow the panels

name: Test Primer
pitch: New engine cover, sidepods and front wing in flat test-part grey.
reference: Unpainted new parts on test cars (Aston Martin AMR26, Barcelona shakedown, January 2026). No photo in the library.
verdict: iterate later: box masks do not follow the part boundaries

name: Heat-Stained Rear
pitch: Paint scorched to straw, purple and blue around the exhaust exit only.
reference: Engine-cover heat staining on McLaren MCL33 and Sauber C32 (f1technical.net threads). No photo in the library.
verdict: iterate later: plausible, but the stain is not tied to the exhaust geometry

name: Sun Faded
pitch: Oxidised single-stage paint: pastel and chalky, the sun-facing top faded most.
reference: Oxidised single-stage paint (Mike Phillips). No photo in the library.
verdict: drop: plausible on a road car, odd on an F1 car
